Note::NlpAccessor::mask_mentions¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::mask_mentions() const

Mask Standalone Handles Without Damaging Email Addresses¶

mask_mentions() replaces an @ handle with [MENTION] when the @ is at the beginning of a cell or follows a non-word byte. The handle body must contain one or more ASCII letters, digits, or underscores. This permits @root, [@alice], and tag:@ann, while protecting x@y.io and mid@name because their @ follows a word byte.

The boundary byte is retained, as is punctuation after the handle. A bare @ is unchanged. The method does not resolve whether a handle exists, decode non-ASCII account names, or infer a person from ordinary prose. It performs a deterministic syntax replacement.

The operation is Text-only, shape-preserving, non-mutating, and idempotent. It creates a fresh packed Text result. Cells without @ take a fast no-match path. Undefined input remains undefined; a defined empty shape remains empty.

Example 1: Valid Handles And Protected Email Syntax¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"@root [@alice], tag:@ann; x@y.io mid@name"})
        .nlp().mask_mentions()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["[MENTION] [[MENTION]], tag:[MENTION]; x@y.io mid@name"]

Example 2: Empty, Undefined, And Bytes¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{})
                       .nlp().mask_mentions();
std::cout << "mentions empty dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel() << '\n';
std::cout << "mentions undefined=" << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().mask_mentions().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"@ann"}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1})
      .nlp().mask_mentions();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "mentions Bytes: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

mentions empty dim=1 numel=0
mentions undefined=false
mentions Bytes: rejected
